items.text: OK, I'm not proud of it, but sometimes when I'm watching TV, I might not actually be watching.
Sometimes I'm just more tempted by my phone.
Be honest, do you do the same?
If you do, then we're not alone, lots of us watch TV with our phones in our hands.
How is TV changing to accommodate this?
Let's start by looking at the data.
Studies have investigated different countries across the world and many of them reported that most people use their phone while watching TV.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that most people use their phone while watching TV

items.text: While the classic stereotype is that it's younger people who find it hard to put their phone down, the data actually shows that second-screening is common in most age groups under 55.

items.text: Younger age groups are more likely to be looking at social media or food delivery apps, while older age groups prefer banking, e-commerce and travel.

level1.label: 状语从句
level1.text: while older age groups prefer banking, e-commerce and travel

items.text: How are producers dealing with this?
A number of screenwriters have reported being told that they need to make programmes easier to follow for distracted viewers.

level2.label: 宾语从句

items.text: Reports say that showrunners have asked for more exposition in dialogue, repetition of plot points and increased use of voice-over to make things clearer for those who aren't looking.

items.text: Some critics and viewers have complained that this could be making series less complex and dialogue less natural.

items.text: Second screens are not the only reason that these things happen.

items.text: Television drama writing developed from radio drama writing, which has to use dialogue to compensate for the lack of visuals.
When books are adapted for TV or film, one challenge is how to tell the whole story with less narration.

items.text: All this means that exposition has often been a feature of TV writing.

items.text: As series became more prestigious and cinematic since the early 2000s, this clear signposting of plot points had become less common.

items.text: Of course, TV viewers and TV programmes are not all the same.
There is space for both casual and more complex programmes.
Maybe the most important thing is for us to remember when to put our phones down.
